leads.claim: The Army Air Forces allegedly recovered remains of a crashed flying disc near Roswell, New Mexico, in July 1947.
leads.why: This is the central claim of the document, involving specific alleged recovery of physical craft material by military personnel.
leads.claimant: Various authors and popular literature cited by the Air Force report.
leads.custody_chain: Recovered by Army Air Forces at Roswell, then allegedly shipped to other locations for analysis.
leads.government_response: The Air Force conducted research and found no records of a cover-up or recovery of extraterrestrial materials, concluding the debris was from a Project Mogul balloon.
leads.quote: Army Air Forces (AAF) allegedly recovered remains of a crashed flying disc

leads.claim: At a second crash site, alleged bodies of extraterrestrial aliens were supposedly retrieved.
leads.why: The claim specifies the recovery of biological entities in addition to craft debris, which is a core component of the Roswell narrative being investigated.
leads.custody_chain: Allegedly retrieved by the AAF and shipped to Wright Field for analysis.
leads.government_response: Air Force research did not disclose any records of the recovery of any alien bodies.
leads.quote: at the second site, alleged bodies of extraterrestrial aliens were supposedly retrieved.

doc_verdict: The document concludes that the alleged recovery of extraterrestrial craft and biological material is a myth, identifying the physical debris as remnants of a Project Mogul balloon.
